chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from al-Hasan ibnasan ibn Ali from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad from a man from our companions called Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The prayer is complete in three places: in the Sacred Mosque, and the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and by the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Where is the prayer considered complete according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the unique spiritual status of the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (AS) in Karbala, elevating it to the same legal standing as the two holiest sites in Islam for the completeness of prayer. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes Karbala as a distinct locus of worship, reflecting the enduring legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt and the significance of martyrdom in connecting the believer to the divine. The inclusion of these three sites underscores the continuity of prophetic and imamic authority across Mecca, Medina, and Karbala.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from a man from our companions called Husayn, 
(It has also been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Salaat is complete in three places – in the Masjid of Al-Harram, and the Masjid of the Rasoolsaww, and by the grave of Al-Husaynasws’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Ibrahim ibn abu al- Balad from a man of our people called Husayn who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Salat (prayer) can be performed in complete form in three places:
‘You should perform salat (prayer) in complete form in Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Masjid), the Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, and in the shrine of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
